findings.summary: The condition lowering's mixed native/browser comparison continuation became unreachable once the binary arm answers for resolved operands; the block now folds or refuses, and the refusal keeps naming the browser operands of any binary expression, because the census locates the unanswered operand from that list.

One helper decides whether an expression over browser operands stays browser state, asked lazily so the first unanswered operand answers before the other operand or the whole is folded; the same rule, narrowed to receivers answered with a primitive, owns member reads and calls, so a lower-cased query string lowers natively.
The value lowering materializes an answered browser chain before the native operator arms see its null half, as it already did for names and calls.
One predicate names the browser values with a native spelling, replacing the inline kind list in the helper-argument classification.

The fixture harness defaults the deployment query to the compiler's own empty search and seeds it on both sides without a fork; the fixture lines that pinned pre-existing folds (a decided short-circuit statement, a split logical condition) are gone.
A nested chain of browser operands folds once per nesting level, quadratic in the chain length (about five folds per squared operand count; 59 to 138 ms at 64 operands).
findings.blockedBy: At real widths of two to six operands the extra folds cost under a millisecond per scene; a per-ask fold memo needs call-scoped invalidation, because bindings change between statements and readsBrowserState re-enters the predicate from inside a fold.
findings.filedIn: TODO.md (the classification consolidation entry: a nested browser-operand chain folds once per node)

findings.summary: The declaration path binds a browser primitive the deployment answers as a browser binding instead of the native constant it materializes to, so every consumer re-derives answered-equals-native and a later assignment to such a name refuses.
findings.blockedBy: Binding the constant changes the generated code of about 85 query bindings across the corpus, upstream and example scenes: a regeneration with its own neutrality proof.

findings.summary: The devicePixelRatio exemption in the binary arm would disappear if the identifier were never browser state, since it has a native lowering of its own.
findings.blockedBy: Removing the identifier from the browser globals changes the value path of every devicePixelRatio read, which needs its own generated-tree proof.
